title: Rights group records 1,445 incidents against minorities in 10 months
excerpt: The Human Rights Congress for Bangladesh Minorities says it recorded 1,445 incidents against religious, ethnic and Indigenous minorities from January to October 2026.
content:
The Human Rights Congress for Bangladesh Minorities (HRCBM), a rights group, says it documented 1,445 incidents affecting religious, ethnic and Indigenous minority communities in all 64 districts between 1 January and 31 October 2026. The report, "The Persecution Continues", was posted on ReliefWeb on Thursday (26 November).

According to HRCBM's summary, the incidents include 286 reported murders and unexplained deaths, 408 attacks on homes, land and other property, 251 attacks on temples or other religious sites and acts of religious vandalism, and 30 blasphemy-related incidents in 14 districts. The report also lists missing-person cases, abductions, physical assaults and sexual violence. HRCBM calls the figures "documented minimums" and says fear of retaliation and stigma lead to underreporting, especially of sexual violence.

The report describes how disputed allegations of religious insult can lead to arrests and retaliation against families, how land grabbing and intimidation push families to leave their homes, and how delays in registering complaints, weak investigations and threats against witnesses block justice. HRCBM calls for equal protection, impartial investigations, remedies and a role for affected communities in transitional justice, and says some patterns warrant independent examination as possible crimes against humanity.

The figures are HRCBM's own. Devlens has not independently verified the incidents, and the report does not separate incidents by motive in its summary. HRCBM says the full report sets out its verification method, district tables and case accounts.

Why it matters

Minority and Indigenous communities often depend on NGOs and legal aid groups to register complaints and reach the courts. Land disputes and attacks on property, the largest category in the report, are areas where legal aid, documentation and local mediation programmes work. Official, independently checked data on such incidents remain scarce.

What to watch

  • Any response from the Home Ministry or the National Human Rights Commission.
  • Human Rights Day on 10 December, when rights groups publish annual figures (see the Events page).

Sources

  • HRCBM via ReliefWeb: The Persecution Continues: Minority Communities Under Sustained Attack in Bangladesh (January - October 2026), 26 November 2026
